nodes.summary: `α̂ = 1 - NI`, for all real counts (the junk values of division agree).
nodes.title: Adaptive proportion estimator equals one minus the neutrality index

nodes.summary: (Smith & Eyre-Walker 2002): `1 - (E D_s E P_n) / (E D_n E P_s) = A / E D_n`.
nodes.title: `α̂` at the expected counts is the proportion of adaptive substitutions

nodes.summary: The Smith–Eyre-Walker estimator of the proportion of adaptive nonsynonymous substitutions, `α̂ = 1 - (D_s P_n) / (D_n P_s)`.
nodes.title: Smith–Eyre-Walker estimator of adaptive substitutions

nodes.summary: The proportion of nonsynonymous substitutions that are adaptive, `α = A / E D_n`.
nodes.title: Proportion of adaptive nonsynonymous substitutions

nodes.summary: Expected nonsynonymous fixed differences `E D_n = λ_D f₀ L_n + A`.
nodes.title: Expected nonsynonymous fixed differences

nodes.summary: Expected synonymous fixed differences `E D_s = λ_D L_s`.
nodes.title: Expected synonymous fixed differences

nodes.summary: Expected nonsynonymous polymorphisms `E P_n = θ_P f₀ L_n`.
nodes.title: Expected nonsynonymous polymorphisms

nodes.summary: Expected synonymous polymorphisms `E P_s = θ_P L_s`.
nodes.title: Expected synonymous polymorphisms

nodes.summary: Expected counts of the MK table without a slightly deleterious class (see the module docstring): synonymous and nonsynonymous mutational targets `Ls`, `Ln`, neutral fraction `f₀` of nonsynonymous mutations, polymorphisms and neutral fixed differences per unit of neutral target `polyRate`, `divRate` (`θ_P`, `λ_D` in the module docstring), and `A` expected adaptive substitutions.
nodes.title: Expected-count model of the McDonald–Kreitman table

nodes.summary: The proportions of nonsynonymous changes among expected fixed differences and expected polymorphisms agree iff there are no adaptive substitutions.
nodes.title: The MK null is neutrality

nodes.summary: Let `Dn i, Ds i, Pn i, Ps i` be the counts at locus `i`; suppose each of the four sequences consists of pairwise independent, identically distributed, integrable variables whose means are the expected counts of `M` (the loci are exchangeable copies of the model). Then almost surely `α̂` computed from the counts summed over the first `m` loci converges to `α = A / E D_n` as `m → ∞`.
nodes.title: Consistency of `α̂` over loci
